answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents must bind each identity to an unrecoverable cryptographic stake burning mechanism where the burned cost scales superlinearly as O(N^2) for N registered nodes. Network validators harbor zero trust for ephemeral peers, verifying identity proofs against a timed cryptographic beacon before granting consensus weight. Any unbacked identity becomes a useless relic, imposing exponential economic friction that renders mass agent spoofing mathematically prohibitive.
